assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of social preferences that reshaped experimental, labor, and organizational economics.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt provide the central inequity-aversion formulation, with Falk making major complementary contributions to reciprocity and experimental evidence.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical and empirical program has been tested extensively across settings over several decades.
uncertainties: The relative boundary between this contribution and earlier behavioral and experimental economics remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel methods made credible empirical work feasible in a vast range of economic applications.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are directly associated with the core estimator; Blundell's contribution to the extended system-GMM framework is central.
assessment.maturity: The methods are exceptionally mature, widely used, and their limitations are also well understood.
uncertainties: The prize-worthy contribution is methodological, and practical misuse of the estimators complicates assessment of their empirical legacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression supplied an enduring framework for studying heterogeneous conditional relationships beyond average effects.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett have unusually clear priority for the defining contribution.
assessment.maturity: The approach has had long-run theoretical development and broad application throughout economics and statistics.
uncertainties: Its impact is diffuse across fields, which may make its economic-sciences framing less immediately salient.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and its geographic determinants.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the linked mobility program; Friedman made important collaborative contributions to its data and empirical architecture.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated a substantial, influential research program and policy debate over more than a decade.
uncertainties: Attribution is complicated by broad research-team contributions and by overlap with earlier mobility scholarship.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection became a central organizing framework for modern trade analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the clearest source of the canonical model, while Helpman and Redding made major related theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has accumulated extensive empirical use and remains central to trade research.
uncertainties: The appropriate allocation of credit across the broader heterogeneous-firm trade literature is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and measurement substantially advanced understanding of selection and welfare in insurance markets.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are prominent empirical architects of the field; Salanie's theoretical and econometric work is highly relevant.
assessment.maturity: A large body of follow-on evidence has tested and refined the approach across insurance settings.
uncertainties: The contribution is a connected research program rather than a single sharply delimited discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made transparent uncertainty under weak assumptions a central econometric principle.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the field-defining originator; Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to moment-inequality methods and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The framework is theoretically mature and has influenced empirical practice where point identification is untenable.
uncertainties: Its practical uptake is narrower than that of some other econometric advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioral game theory established laboratory evidence as a powerful source of economic knowledge.
assessment.attribution: Plott and Holt made foundational experimental-market contributions, while Camerer helped establish behavioral game theory and its broader influence.
assessment.maturity: The program is longstanding and has produced a large body of replications, extensions, and methodological refinement.
uncertainties: Credit is difficult to delimit because many foundational experimental economists contributed and prior recognition covers part of the field.
